question: Can one bounded positive context-glare fraction inferred from a development scanner transfer to a different laboratory scanner of the same disclosed hardware family and polarity, rather than treating scanner/lab processing as film response?
claim_ceiling: measured-table scanner-context nuisance transfer evidence for one ARRI AQUA/Kodak 2254 test leader; not a scanner calibration, named stock response, inverse glare correction, arbitrary-film result or product profile

primary_source.title: Tonal distribution and glare assessment in cinematographic film scanners
primary_source.reported_test_material: ARRI AQUA 2017 test leader printed on KODAK Color Digital Intermediate Film 2254
primary_source.reported_measurement: Table 3 Context Glare ratio and difference for positive and negative scans
primary_source.data_availability_statement: No datasets were generated or analysed during the current study.

measurement_protocol.undefined_ratio_or_negative_difference_p: retain row facts but exclude from positive-fraction fitting and scoring

explicit_operator.domain: relative scanner-linear black and white-context signal
explicit_operator.f_estimator: f = (B_c - B_v) / (1 - B_v), development row only
explicit_operator.candidate: same-hardware development f transferred unchanged to confirmation scanners of the same disclosed hardware family and scan polarity

branch_rule.pass: Retain a generic same-hardware context-glare transfer hypothesis and open a separate synthetic spatial-kernel compiler; no scanner profile or product mapping.
branch_rule.fail: Close cross-lab/hardware-family transfer for this one-fraction operator, retain scanner/lab/polarity as nuisance and continue a distinct physical-film mechanism without model or threshold rescue.

forbidden: post-result scanner split, row exclusion, fraction bound or threshold changes
treat context glare or scanner processing as film stock response or latent mode
fit or remove glare from article figures or embedded raster illustrations
pool positive and negative scan encodings
claim measured glare spread function, scanner calibration or inverse restoration
operator fitting to photographs, product integration, training or visual promotion
